title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Valparaíso: find fast!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race from both start and destination across a street-graph model of Valparaíso (Cerro Alegre). The moment the two frontiers meet, the shortest path emerges with fewer explored nodes than classic one-way search.
ig_caption:
🚠🌊 **Valparaíso map run (Cerro Alegre) using Bidirectional Dijkstra**

In this visualization, we treat real streets as a **weighted graph** (nodes = intersections, edges = road segments with costs like distance/turn penalties). **Bidirectional Dijkstra** launches two priority queues: one expanding from the **start** and one expanding from the **goal**—each guaranteed to grow in nondecreasing path cost. ✅ When the expanding frontiers meet at a shared node/edge boundary, the algorithm stitches the partial shortest paths into the overall minimum-cost route.

🧠 Graph theory highlights: it’s a **shortest-path search** on a weighted graph where optimality comes from Dijkstra’s relaxation invariant, while efficiency improves by reducing the explored search radius.

yt_description:
Bidirectional Dijkstra on real street maps in Valparaíso (Cerro Alegre)! 🌊🚠

In this YouTube Shorts visualization, we convert a neighborhood street layout into a weighted graph (intersections + road segments), then run **Bidirectional Dijkstra** using two synchronized priority queues. The path is found when forward and backward searches meet, producing an optimal shortest route with fewer explored nodes than one-direction search.
